Agriculture Domain - Market and Trade Regulations

Agricultural market and trade activities are governed by market regulations, banking laws, food safety standards, and export-import regulations.

For Crop Selling Registration: Required attributes include seller name (farmer/trader), farmer ID or trader license, crop type and variety, quantity, quality grade, harvest date, farm location, and bank account for payment. Market fee payment information. Transportation details if applicable.

For Market Price Information: Required attributes include crop type, market location, date, wholesale price, retail price (if available), quality grade, and transaction volume (aggregated). Individual seller/buyer information is NOT required for price information services - only aggregated market data. Price information is typically public data.

For Agricultural Loan: Required attributes include borrower name, identity proof, land ownership/lease documents, crop details, loan amount, purpose, collateral information, repayment terms, bank account for disbursement, and credit assessment data. KYC documents per banking regulations. Income/asset verification for larger loans.

For Produce Quality Certificate: Required attributes include producer name and identification, crop type and variety, quantity, quality testing results (moisture, grade, contamination tests), inspection date, inspector identifier, and certificate validity period. Farm location. Certification standard (organic, fair trade, etc.) if applicable.

For Export License: Required attributes include exporter name and registration, product type and quantity, destination country, phytosanitary certificate, quality certificate, customs documentation, and licensing authority approval. Importer information. Trade agreement compliance documentation.

UNNECESSARY Attributes: Religion, ethnicity, political affiliation are unnecessary for market/trade purposes. Email is optional unless digital notifications are requested. Social media profiles are not required.

Food Safety: Produce quality certificates must comply with food safety standards (FDA, USDA, or equivalent). Export licenses must meet destination country import requirements.

Banking Regulations: Agricultural loans must comply with banking KYC and lending regulations. Interest rates may be regulated by agricultural credit policies.
